description: Point it at LinkedIn person profiles or company pages and it returns the posts a search engine has indexed for each one, as flat rows: permalink, author, a text excerpt, and the publish date decoded from the post id. No request is sent to LinkedIn and no cookie or account is used. A result counts only when its permalink names the source, so posts are never attributed to the wrong author. Coverage is what the search index holds: posts appear days or weeks after publishing and many never appear. Commenters, reaction counts, comment counts and media are no longer returned (removed 2026-10-12, they came only from LinkedIn pages). Rows carry row_type post or notice; filter on row_type before loading a table. post_id is the activity URN and is stable across runs. Every row carries degraded and degradation_reason. Requires an APIFY_TOKEN and consumes Apify credits. Read only.

company_urls.description: LinkedIn company page URLs, for example https://www.linkedin.com/company/microsoft. Supply this, profile_urls, or both.

max_charge_usd.description: Optional. The actor's own spend cap for this run, in USD. The run stops before a charge would take its total past this amount, writes one notice row saying so, and keeps every row already charged. Leave it empty for no cap of your own; the maximum cost per run set in Apify is honored either way.

posted_since.description: ISO date or timestamp, for example 2026-08-01. Posts published before this are skipped BEFORE anything is charged. Leave empty to take everything the index holds.

profile_urls.description: LinkedIn person profile URLs, for example https://www.linkedin.com/in/williamhgates. Country subdomains such as uk.linkedin.com are fine. Supply this, company_urls, or both.

name: capture_linkedin_posts_and_commenters
title: Capture LinkedIn Posts and Commenters
